answer: A fingerprint registry stops clones. First, an agent submits a hash and sample of 2 GB of data; fingerprints over 90% similar to an entry are rejected. Second, anyone may challenge within 7 days, and a verifier re-runs the check. Third, disputed identities freeze until they pass with new data; repeat offenders lose their slot for 30 days. A Sybil farm is a grove cloned from one root, each honest agent an island of data; a velvet rope stops no forger. At $5 per GB, one identity costs $10, so 1,000 Sybils cost $10,000. Like a library rejecting a second copy, it admits only new volumes.
